## Why
Workers open **draft** PRs (SKILL.md step 5). `hkb complete` found the open PR #12 and moved #1 to `review` — but left the PR a draft, so `gh pr merge` failed with "Pull Request is still a draft". The human had to run `gh pr ready` first. The terminal verb must leave the PR mergeable.

## What
- In `src/lifecycle.js`, when `complete` or `request-review` finds an open PR referencing the task (`task.prs`), mark it ready for review via GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview(input:{pullRequestId})` (needs the PR node id — add it to the `closedByPullRequestsReferences` selection in `src/tasks.js`). Do nothing if it is already non-draft.
- `request-review --reviewer <login>` additionally requests that GitHub user as a reviewer (`POST pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers`) when the login exists; ignore profiles that are not GitHub users.
- Record `pr` and `pr_head` (head ref name) on the attempt row in the run comment.
- Pure-function test for the decision (draft → mark ready; open → skip; none → skip); no live calls.

## Done when
After `hkb complete <n>` with a draft PR, `gh pr view` shows it ready for review and `gh pr merge --squash` succeeds.
title: complete/request-review must mark the task's draft PR ready for review
